original_question: In the setting of Theorem 3.5, let Omega be a C^{3,1} smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let phi belong to C^{3,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, solving (dd^c u)^n = f in Omega with f >= 0 and f^{1/n} in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). Determine the minimal assumptions under which u belongs to C^2(closure Omega).
target_in_paper: Question 26 in Section 3.6, immediately after Theorem 3.5 (Krylov) and the Bedford–Fornæss remark that C^2(Ω̄) can fail under the Theorem 3.5 hypotheses. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly imports the exact ambient local Monge–Ampère Dirichlet setting used in Theorem 3.5: Ω ⊂ ℂ^n, Ω C^{3,1}-smooth, strictly pseudoconvex, bounded; φ ∈ C^{3,1}(∂Ω); u the unique plurisubharmonic solution continuous on Ω̄; and f ≥ 0 with f^{1/n} ∈ C^{1,1}(Ω̄). It also correctly identifies that the real issue is the jump from Krylov’s C^{1,1}(Ω̄) conclusion to C^2(Ω̄), which is exactly what Question 26 asks about. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The boundary condition u = φ on ∂Ω should be stated explicitly. In the paper this is part of the problem data in both Question 25 and Theorem 3.5. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

To match the paper’s actual intent, the question should ask for the minimal additional assumptions ensuring u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), because the Theorem 3.5 assumptions alone are not sufficient. The paper states this immediately after noting the Bedford–Fornæss counterexample. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

A fully stand-alone version should say that (dd^c u)^n is the complex Monge–Ampère measure in the paper’s local notation; when u is smooth, this is a normalized determinant density with respect to Lebesgue volume. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

If one wants the equation written as a measure equation rather than the paper’s shorthand, one should specify that f is the nonnegative density on Ω (or Ω̄, since f^{1/n} is assumed on Ω̄) appearing on the right-hand side of the local Monge–Ampère equation. Nearby local questions in Section 3 write this explicitly as f dV. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The paper does not ask for a characterization in a broader class of domains or weaker regularity scales; it keeps the scope tightly tied to the exact Theorem 3.5 setting. So the refined question should stay local, strictly pseudoconvex, bounded, and up-to-the-boundary. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a C^{3,1}-smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain, let φ ∈ C^{3,1}(∂Ω), and let u ∈ PSH(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄) be the unique solution of the Dirichlet problem u = φ on ∂Ω and (dd^c u)^n = f in Ω, where f ≥ 0 and f^{1/n} ∈ C^{1,1}(Ω̄). Krylov’s theorem yields u ∈ C^{1,1}(Ω̄), while Bedford–Fornæss show that these hypotheses do not in general force u ∈ C^2(Ω̄). What are the minimal additional assumptions under which one can guarantee that u belongs to C^2(Ω̄)? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the open problem labeled Question 26, not at proving Theorem 3.5 itself: it reproduces the Theorem 3.5 hypotheses and then asks for the threshold for C^2 regularity. Section 3.6 first discusses Krylov’s C^{1,1} regularity in Question 25, then states Theorem 3.5 (up-to-the-boundary C^{1,1}), then immediately records that C^2 can fail under those hypotheses and asks Question 26. So the paper-faithful sharpening is: find the minimal strengthening of the Theorem 3.5 assumptions that guarantees C^2 regularity up to the boundary. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
